articles.title: Piloto é alertado por motorista de ônibus sobre moto em chamas em MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Motorista percebeu as chamas na parte traseira da moto e fez manobras para chamar a atenção do motociclista; vídeo do episódio já soma mais de 1,1 milhão de visualizações nas redes sociais.
articles.summary: Motorista percebeu as chamas na parte traseira da moto; vídeo do episódio já soma mais de 1,1 milhão de visualizações nas redes sociais.
articles.body:
Um criador de conteúdo registrou o momento em que foi alertado por um motorista de ônibus sobre um princípio de incêndio em um alforge instalado na parte traseira da moto que pilotava (assista acima) . O caso aconteceu próximo à região urbana de Porto Estrela , a 198 km de Cuiabá, de acordo com a última localidade identificada na gravação.

O vídeo foi publicado no perfil “Carlos Aventuras de Moto” no YouTube e no Instagram, utilizado pelo motociclista para compartilhar conteúdos de viagens e pilotagens, no último sábado (12). Nas imagens, é possível ver as chamas no alforge, na parte traseira da moto, depois que o veículo para no acostamento.

O g1 tentou contato com o responsável pelo perfil, mas mas ele não quis se pronunciar sobre o caso.

Conforme descrito no vídeo publicado pelo motociclista, o motorista do ônibus fez cerca de três manobras para tentar chamar sua atenção. Em um primeiro momento, ele interpretou a atitude como imprudência, conforme relatado em uma legenda inserida no vídeo.

Depois que os veículos pararam próximo ao acostamento, o motorista do ônibus e outros passageiros desceram para alertar o motociclista sobre o fogo. Em seguida, eles ajudaram a controlar as chamas, utilizando água e abafando o fogo.

Em outro trecho da gravação, o motorista afirma que, se o motociclista tivesse parado no primeiro sinal, as chamas poderiam ter sido evitadas.

O motorista do ônibus foi identificado como Reinaldo. De acordo com Uvander Lechner, gerente de tráfego da Viação Juína, ele é morador de Cáceres e trabalha na rota entre Cáceres e Tangará da Serra .

Ainda segundo o gerente, Reinaldo percebeu o fogo que saía da região do escapamento da moto e tentou alertar o motociclista para que parasse no acostamento. Para Uvander, a atitude do motorista ajudou a evitar uma possível tragédia.

Após o ocorrido, o motociclista aparece no vídeo relatando que ficou com um sentimento de vergonha e decepção diante da situação. Ele também afirma que a viagem que estava realizando não deveria ter acontecido.

O vídeo do episódio já soma mais de 1,1 milhão de visualizações nas redes sociais. Em publicação realizada nesta terça-feira (15), o motociclista agradeceu a ajuda recebida, respondeu às críticas e afirmou que não pretende responder a ofensas enviadas por mensagens privadas.

O motociclista também assumiu a responsabilidade pelo ocorrido e reconheceu que errou ao não parar quando foi alertado pelo motorista do ônibus. Ele pediu desculpas publicamente a Reinaldo e explicou que não reagiu no primeiro momento porque ficou em estado de choque.

articles.title: Sale a la venta la Ducati con la que Valentino Rossi homenajeó al fallecido Simoncelli
articles.standfirst: La casa londinense Fiskens pone en el mercado esta Ducati GP12.0 de Valentino Rossi y su precio podría alcanzar cifras de récord
articles.summary: La casa londinense Fiskens pone en el mercado la GP12.0 con chasis VR2, una de las cinco unidades construidas y la única moto de MotoGP de Rossi que puede acabar en manos de un particular.
articles.body: La casa Fiskens, especialista en coches históricos con sede en el barrio londinense de Kensington, acaba de incluir en su catálogo una moto que muchos soñarían incluso con solo poder ver de cerca: una Ducati GP12.0 de 2011, con el chasis número VR2. Se trata de la moto de pruebas y desarrollo que Valentino Rossi utilizó durante su etapa en el equipo oficial italiano, y el propio vendedor la describe como el equivalente sobre dos ruedas al Ferrari de Michael Schumacher. Para entender el valor de esta moto conviene recordar el ambiente que se vivía en Borgo Panigale en aquel otoño de 2011. El fichaje de Rossi por Ducati había despertado una expectación enorme en Italia, con la idea de que el piloto más laureado del momento devolvería a la marca de Bolonia al lugar que merecía. Pero no. La realidad resultó bastante más dura, y a la altura de septiembre la fábrica ya había introducido tres cambios radicales en la GP11, mientras Rossi seguía sin adaptarse a la moto. Ante ese callejón, el desarrollo de la GP12 se aceleró antes incluso de que terminara la temporada 2011. Y ahí llegó el gran giro; por insistencia del propio Rossi, el equipo oficial abandonó el chasis de fibra de carbono en el que había invertido millones de euros y pasó a un bastidor de doble viga de aluminio. Una decisión que reconocía, en la práctica, que la enorme apuesta técnica de la casa resultaba imposible de pilotar al límite. De aquella hornada se construyeron solo cinco GP12.0, reservadas en exclusiva para Rossi y Nicky Hayden, campeón del mundo de MotoGP en 2006 y fallecido en 2017. Rossi lideró todo el trabajo de pruebas, experimentando con distintas configuraciones de chasis y geometrías de suspensión. Las fotografías en un test de Mugello en septiembre, sumadas a unos planos CAD de los nuevos bastidores que acabaron filtrándose, alimentaron durante semanas las conjeturas sobre lo que Ducati preparaba para 2012. La confirmación llegó en el test de noviembre, apenas un día después de que cayera la bandera a cuadros en Valencia para cerrar la temporada, cuando las GP12.0 se mostraron al completo con su bastidor de aluminio a la vista. La moto que ves, con el bastidor VR2, estuvo presente en ambas sesiones y quedó retratada hasta la saciedad junto al siete veces campeón de MotoGP. Pero, como recordarás, aquel año el paddock había encajado uno de sus golpes más duros con la muerte de Marco Simoncelli en un accidente durante el Gran Premio de Malasia. Con la atención mediática desbordada en el test valenciano, Rossi aprovechó el foco para un rendir un homenaje a su amigo, colocando en persona el dorsal 58 de Simoncelli sobre su propio 46 del carenado y enfundándose un casco que honraba a su paisano. Todo aquello quedó inmortalizado con esta moto. La vida deportiva de esta moto continuó al año siguiente cuando fue cedida a Karel Abraham para disputar el Mundial de 2012, con el chasis rebautizado como KA2. En la última carrera de aquel curso, de nuevo en Valencia, la moto se apuntó el honor de terminar como la Ducati mejor clasificada de la parrilla. Y al acabar el campeonato regresó al equipo oficial, con toda la trazabilidad certificada por la propia fábrica. Desde allí pasó a manos de un coleccionista privado, en estado de marcha y acompañada de todas las piezas asociadas a los test de 2011, donde se reunió con dos GP12.0 antaño pilotadas por Hayden. Ya dentro de esa colección, la moto pasó por un proceso de restauración minucioso para devolverle los componentes exactos que Rossi probó y desarrolló en su día. Para entender su importancia, debemos tener en cuenta que Yamaha y Honda destruyen la inmensa mayoría de sus motos de MotoGP, al considerarlas material amortizado de investigación y desarrollo, de modo que ninguna de ellas circula por el mercado de coleccionistas. Ese detalle convierte a esta Ducati en una de las poquísimas oportunidades existentes para hacerse con una moto de Gran Premio pilotada por Rossi. Fiskens la ofrece en condiciones de funcionamiento tras una reconstrucción realizada por la propia Ducati, lo que abre la puerta a algo más que exhibirla en un salón y más bien invita a rodar con ella en circuito. El precio, por desgracia, no lo dan más que a los realmente interesados y por privado. Sin embargo, en mayo de 2012 RM Auctions sacó a subasta en Mónaco dos Desmosedici cedidas por el propio departamento de Ducati Corse, y la GP11 que Rossi pilotó aquella temporada alcanzó los 245.700 euros, mientras que la GP10 ganadora de Casey Stoner se quedó en 251.550 euros. Pero desde aquellas ventas la retirada de Rossi en 2021 disparó el valor de todo lo asociado a su figura, además de que ha subido el mercado de motos históricas de competición (una MV Agusta 500 de Gran Premio de 1965 cambió de manos este mismo año por 1.141.000 euros, rozando el récord absoluto para una moto en subasta. Por ello, una horquilla razonable para esta GP12.0 se movería entre los 400.000 y los 700.000 euros.

articles.title: Formula 1 2027: Calendar to have 10 sprint races next year, including Monaco
articles.summary: Formula 1 increases the number of sprint races from six to 10 for the 2027 World Championship.
articles.body:
Formula 1 has increased the number of sprint races from six to 10 for the 2027 World Championship.

Sprint events, which feature a shorter race on Saturday and an extra qualifying session on Friday, will be held for the first time in Bahrain, Australia, Japan, Monaco, and Abu Dhabi.

The other sprints will be in Canada, Britain, Italy, Brazil, and Qatar, it was revealed as the calendar was formally announced.

The maximum number of sprints previously in a season has been six.

The 2027 season is scheduled to start in Bahrain on 12-14 March, followed by Saudi Arabia a week later, but both events will remain in doubt while the war in the Middle East continues.

Bahrain is the default season-opening race, but Australia has hosted the first grand prix for the past two years because of the timing of the Muslim holy month of Ramadan.

The 2026 season is due to end with two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, and while F1 is planning to complete the calendar as scheduled, it is working on contingency plans if those races cannot be held as a result of the continuing conflict between the US/Israel and Iran.

The same applies for the start of next season as F1 considers its options for an alternative opening schedule if racing in the Middle East looks impossible by the end of this year.

On Sunday, a summit involving some of the nations involved in or affected by the conflict released a statement urging "maximum restraint" in the war.

The British Grand Prix will be on 2-4 July, and the 2027 season re-introduces races in Portugal and Turkey, returning for the first time since being used as placeholder events during the pandemic.

Sprint events usually come at a higher price for race organisers but they are in demand because they increase the chance of selling more tickets, with competitive action on each of the three days of the meeting rather than only Saturday and Sunday.

Silverstone believe holding a sprint this year was a large part of the reason for the British Grand Prix’s highest ever attendance - 64,000 more fans attended over the course of the four days compared with the year before, which was not a sprint.

The inclusion of a sprint event in Monaco will inevitably raise eyebrows, given it is almost impossible to overtake around the historic street circuit.

However, F1 is selling it on the fact that it means there will be two qualifying sessions at Monaco - qualifying around the demanding track is renowned as one of the highlights of the season.

Two separate qualifying sessions could also provide two different grid orders, increasing variability.

The flip side of a sprint in Monaco is that, because of the lack of overtaking opportunities, the finishing order of the sprint will be pretty much locked in once the cars have completed the first lap, barring accidents.

F1 president and chief executive officer Stefano Domenicali said: "We are thrilled to welcome Portugal and Turkey to the championship and to expand sprint racing to 10 events, giving our fans even more intensity, drama, and the wheel-to-wheel action that make our sport so special."

Mohammed Ben Sulayem, the president of F1's governing body the FIA, said: "The 2027 FIA F1 World Championship calendar is a strong reflection of the global appeal and continued growth of our sport.

"With 24 grands prix across five continents, the return of Portugal and Turkey, and the opportunity for an expanded sprint programme, the calendar combines tradition, innovation and fan engagement while maintaining the highest sporting standards."

Pre-season testing is also scheduled to be held in Bahrain on 24-27 February.

articles.title: Hay ya calendario F1 2027, con Madring del 10 al 12 de septiembre y sin Barcelona
articles.standfirst: Los test de pretemporada serán de nuevo en Bahrein
articles.summary: Los test de pretemporada serán de nuevo en Bahrein
articles.body: Sin haberse confirmado aún el final de 2026 por el conflicto en el Golfo Pérsico, la F1 ha anunciado este miércoles su calendario oficial para 2027, donde se confirma el GP de España en Madring del 10 al 12 de septiembre. Se especulaba con que podría tomar un lugar antes que Monza, una semana antes que este año, pero se mantiene en la misma semana que la primera edición. Además será un año en el que Barcelona deja de tener prueba por primera vez desde 1991, para alternarse con Spa y regresar luego en años alternos a partir de 2028. También se hablaba de la posibilidades de los test invernales, esta vez de cuatro días y no de tres (como hasta 2025) en Bahréin, como previa a la primera carrera de 2027 en el mismo escenario en Sakhir. Barcelona aparecía como opción, pero se mantiene lo firmado, con esas pruebas y las dos primeras carreras en la zona de Oriente Medio, es decir, Bahréin y Arabia. "La Fórmula 1 y la FIA han anunciado, tras la aprobación del Consejo Mundial del Deporte del Motor, el calendario del Campeonato Mundial de Fórmula 1 de la FIA 2027, que incluye 24 Grandes Premios en 22 países y 10 carreras sprint", ha comunicado hoy la F1 que dirige Stefano Domenicali. "Los test de pretemporada tendrán lugar en Bahréin del 24 al 27 de febrero, antes de que el campeonato regrese a ese país para la primera carrera, seguida de Arabia Saudí. El calendario continuará con Australia, Japón y China, seguidos de los Grandes Premios de Miami y Canadá. La etapa europea incluye el regreso de la Fórmula 1 a Portugal en junio, después de Mónaco, con la reincorporación de Turquía al calendario en octubre, entre Azerbaiyán y Singapur. La fase final de la temporada contará con carreras en Austin, Ciudad de México, São Paulo y Las Vegas, antes de las dos últimas rondas en Qatar y Abu Dabi", certifican, La F1 amplía el formato con prueba Sprint de seis a 10 grandes premios, con una justificación clara. "Debido al éxito continuado y la fuerte demanda del formato, el número de carreras Sprint ha aumentado de seis a diez para 2027, ofreciendo aún más emoción y competitividad durante toda la temporada para aficionados, promotores, cadenas de televisión y patrocinadores", informa la F1. "Desde la introducción de las carreras Sprint en 2021, los datos muestran que la audiencia total de los fines de semana Sprint es un 12 % superior a la de los fines de semana sin Sprint, la Clasificación Sprint es hasta tres veces más popular entre los aficionados que los Entrenamientos Libres, el 82 % de los asistentes a los fines de semana Sprint afirma que aporta valor añadido a su entrada, y el 75 % de los aficionados a la F1 cree que las carreras sprint aportan mayor valor al calendario de la temporada", explican en el comunicado oficial. articles.title: Should NASCAR Teams Have More Freedom After the Brake Failure Disaster?
articles.summary: NASCAR’s Enjoy Illinois 300 at World Wide Technology Raceway was already chaotic. Then the brakes started failing. Ryan Blaney was running […]
articles.body:
NASCAR's Enjoy Illinois 300 at World Wide Technology Raceway was already chaotic. Then the brakes started failing.

Ryan Blaney was running sixth on Lap 155 when the right-front brake rotor on his No.12 Ford exploded. The 2023 Cup champion had been in contention for a strong result, but the failure sent him into the outside wall and ended his race with a 35th-place finish. His crew chief Jonathan Hassler later admitted the team had underestimated how much cooling the brakes needed with NASCAR's higher-horsepower package.

Then, on Lap 214, Chase Elliott who was running sevent, suffered a brake failure while running seventh. His No.9 Chevrolet spun into Chase Briscoe, taking both playoff drivers out of the race.

Then, with just three laps remaining, Chris Buescher suffered another brake failure that brought out the caution and sent the race into overtime.

Those failures and minor mechanical issues have changed the playoff picture.

Only three of the 16 Chase drivers finished the Gateway race in the same position they entered it. Briscoe fell from fifth to eighth in the standings , and Elliott dropped from ninth to 11th. Ryan Blaney also lost ground to points leader Denny Hamlin .

And the brake failures were only part of a race that spiraled into chaos. Gateway produced 18 cautions, two red flags and a double-overtime finish. The 18 yellows shattered the track record and matched the Next Gen-era high.

For Kevin Harvick, that raises a question NASCAR may have to address.

Harvick wants NASCAR to give teams more freedom

Speaking on the Speed with Harvick and Buxton podcast, the 2014 Cup Series champion pointed to the rule that limits what teams can replace after practice and suggested NASCAR reconsider it before next season.

"They had an extended practice, probably need to think about next year, maybe letting them change the pads and the rotors or calipers, whatever they need to change after practice in order to go into the race."

The argument makes sens. Teams had extended practice at Gateway to understand the demands of a track known for heavy braking. If the brake components show excessive wear or teams discover that their cooling setup is not sufficient, Harvick believes they should have the freedom to replace those components before the race.

The 1.25-mile oval features long straightaways followed by heavy braking zones, putting repeated heat cycles through the brakes. The new 2026 package made that challenge even greater, with NASCAR increasing horsepower to 750 at selected tracks while reducing downforce. acknowledged earlier in the season that the extra speed and reduced aerodynamic stability were contributing to additional brake wear.

As of now, the teams can change brake components during the race, but under the current impound rules, they cannot simply replace the brake pads after practice and before the race starts.

At Gateway, teams had an extended one-hour practice. They could use that session to evaluate the brake package, but once practice/qualifying and the impound procedure were complete, the car was effectively locked down. If a team discovered that its brake pads or rotors had been pushed too hard in practice, it couldn't just install a fresh set before Sunday's race.

So, Harvick's proposal would not mean abandoning the 750-horsepower package. His suggestion is much narrower: give teams the freedom to replace brake pads, rotors or calipers after practice, before the race, if the practice session reveals a problem.

Could NASCAR use Gateway's failures as a reason to reconsider how much freedom teams have to protect themselves from another brake disaster?

articles.title: El reto más loco de Verstappen: horario y reglas de su carrera ante 100 rivales en kart
articles.standfirst: El desafío planteado por Red Bull hace que el neerlandés tenga que salir último... y remontar
articles.summary: El desafío planteado por Red Bull hace que el neerlandés tenga que salir último... y remontar
articles.body: Que Max Verstappen se apunta a todo parece un hecho. El neerlandés vcompatibiliza su carrera en la Fórmula 1, en la que relucen las cuatro coronas de campeón, con actuaciones brillantes en GT3 (una avería le dejó sin ganar las últimas 24 Horas de Nurburgring), pruebas con todo tipo de coches de carreras, el sueño de Le Mans (quizá con Alonso como compañero), competiciones profesionales de simulación (iRacing) o de dueño de su propio equipo. Pero ningún reto era tan loco como el que le medirá a 100 pilotos en un circuito... de karts. Nació como una iniciativa de Red Bull para el parón entre Madrid y el triplete que arrancará en Bakú. Max se medirá a 100 pilotos en karts 'de alquiler' en Silverstone y su objetivo será batirlos. Partirá al final del todo de la tabla y se medirá a todo tipo de figuras amateurs, como el streamer español TheGrefg, periodistas, famosos... El reto consta de 30 vueltas en las que tiene que pasar a todos. Según adelante se irán eliminando rivales y cuentan con una carta secreta ante la estrella, una vuelta con atajo. Para Max también existirá, pero sólo puede activarla a partir del giro 15. Los karts son iguales, con 85 kilogramos de peso y el del #3 irá decorado con sus habituales colores de Red Bull. "Será una locura. Llevo bastante sin probar en los go-karts y coincidir con tanta gente será duro", admitió el propio piloto. Aunque su palmarés con los vehículos de iniciación es tremendo, pues cuenta con títulos de campeón europeo y mundial antes de su ascenso a la Fórmula 3, posterior fichaje por Red Bull y salto al estrellato en el que se encuentra ahora mismo instalado. El duelo de Verstappen contra 100 karts se disputará a partir de las 19:00 horas en horario peninsular español con una previa que empezará desde las 18:00 horas. Los derechos de emisión pertenecen a Disney+ o ESPN, y en determinados países habrá retransmisión a través de la plataforma de Red Bull. La parrilla todavía no ha sido confirmada al completo, aunque los primeros nombres indican que no serán profesionales de la competición en las cuatro ruedas. articles.title: La F1 2027 opta por la revolución: Mónaco al sprint, Madring 2.0 y esperando a Alonso
articles.standfirst: Cuando todavía no existe una confirmación de la finalización del curso 2027, el futuro toma fuerza con calendario, reglas... y a la espera de la decisión de Alonso
articles.summary: Cuando todavía no existe una confirmación de la finalización del curso 2027, el futuro toma fuerza con calendario, reglas... y a la espera de la decisión de Alonso
articles.body: Todavía se desconoce cómo terminará la campaña 2026 de la Fórmula 1 y si el Gran Circo podrá cerrar, como tiene previsto, su campaña en Qatar y Abu Dhabi. Las entradas de ambas carreras siguen siendo vendidas a velocidad de vértigo, pero la opción de finalizar en Ímola está en la recámara si no se pudiese por mor del conflicto en el Golfo Pérsico. De cualquiera de las maneras, todavía quedan tres meses de carreras en los que Kimi Antonelli buscará cerrar su enorme campeonato, pero ya hay otra nueva dimensión en la mesa. El 2027 se empezó a dibujar con un calendario que opta por la revolución. La realidad más palpable del nuevo calendario es que el formato sprint está más presente que nunca. Se empieza a completar el anhelo de Stefano Domenicali, CEO de la F1, de avanzar en el desarrollo del formato, con una ampliación a 10 fines de semana. Y no de cualquier forma, pues los habrá en puntos estratégicos. Empezarán para repartir los primeros puntos del año en Bahréin, cambiarán el fin de semana de Mónaco y la temporada también se cerrará con tres en las últimas cuatro citas al introducirlos en Interlagos, Losail y Yas Marina. Es un nuevo planteamiento, más cercano a MotoGP y que buscará dar otro aire a fines de semana claves como el primero, en un Bahréin donde los equipos habrán probado sin cesar en pretemporada, o un Mónaco que tendrá dos clasificaciones en la vuelta más tensa de la temporada que da paso a una carrera con poco movimiento. La tradición se rompe, ahora se juzgará a la revolución. Parada a parada, las novedades en materia de circuitos son dos. El regreso de Portimao, un circuito de sube y baja en el que se han visto carreras bonitas. La cita lusa ocupará la fecha de Barcelona en las últimas temporadas. Y Estambul, otro circuito bonito, con una curva increíble en su 8 y en la línea de una F1 que sigue expandiéndose más allá de las fronteras europeas. Ya no es el continente más visitado. En clave española, Madring repetirá presencia y Montmeló entra en su rotación con Spa. Es el primer curso sin parada en el Circuit desde 1991, con victoria de Nigel Mansell. Para Madrid habrá una segunda edición del Gran Premio de España en la misma fecha (10 al 12 de septiembre), como fin de la gira europea y en una configuración de circuito que será diferente en varias curvas para garantizar un mejor y mayor espectáculo en pista. Las pruebas, además, quedan repartidas de una forma que no se coincidirá con otros grandes eventos del motor, como las 500 Millas de Indianápolis (30 de mayo) o las 24 Horas de Le Mans (9 al 13 de junio). Se abre la opción a ver a pilotos de F1 intentándolo. Max Verstappen tarde o temprano se atreverá a la carrera de resistencia más laureada (además de volver a Nurburgring), Fernando Alonso ha admitido que quiere volver o recientemente Lando Norris probó el nuevo hypercar de McLaren. En clave Fórmula 1, también queda un asunto más que resolver. Si la parrilla muestra un continuismo claro más allá de dudas en asientos como RB (Tsolov entra en las quinielas), Haas (se rumorea que Fornaroli y Camara están en la pole para sustituir a Ocon) o Cadillac, hay una estrella que todavía no ha anunciado nada: Fernando Alonso. Sigue debatiéndose sobre qué decisión tomar con el reglamento de la F1 como centro de sus análisis. Recientemente, recalcó que confiaba en más ajustes de las reglas y podrían ir relacionadas a un impulso al suministrador de unidad de potencia de su equipo, Honda. Tanto Mercedes como Red Bull han dejado claro que no verían con malos ojos ese apoyo. Eso elevaría la competitividad de Alonso. Que bien podría dejar la F1... o ampliar por muchos años más. "Si renuevo puedo hacerlo por muchos años", soltó a MARCA durante el fin de semana de Madring. En la F1 de la revolución es el piloto más veterano y el que sigue faltando por colocar su pieza en el gran tablero de la nueva temporada.

articles.title: Fenómeno Verstappen: sale último y bate a 100 karts... ¡en 13 vueltas!
articles.standfirst: El tetracampeón holandés pasa su reto más especial con suficiencia
articles.summary: El tetracampeón holandés pasa su reto más especial con suficiencia
articles.body: Max Verstappen es un fenómeno inacabable. El neerlandés aprovechó el parón de una semana en la Fórmula 1 entre los Grandes Premios de España y Azerbaiyán para superar su reto más especial. No es ni el título mundial de la clase reina, del que sigue siendo su campeón más joven (a la espera de Kimi Antonelli), ni tampoco su cuenta pendiente con las 24 Horas de Nurburgring tras romper su Mercedes AMG GT3 en 2026 cuando lideraban. Es algo más sencillo. Más especial. Una iniciativa de Red Bull le invitó a medirse a 100 karts (todos iguales, de alquiler), saliendo último y con sólo 30 vueltas de carrera. No le hizo falta ni la mitad de las disponibles. Insuperable para cualquier rival amateur. Verstappen arrasó en el pequeño circuito de karting en Silverstone desde el puesto 101 de la parrilla. En una vuelta ya había adelantado hasta la posición 37 tras salir empujando su pequeña máquina y sobrevivir a la montonera de la primera frenada. A partir de ahí colocó el ritmo machacón y sólo le hicieron falta 13 giros para finalizar el reto. Nada mal para un Max que admitió que llevaba mucho tiempo sin probar los pequeños vehículos de iniciación. En su progresión, el #3 de Red Bull no contó con la posibilidad de atajo que tenían sus rivales, pero sólo sirvió para que la agonía siguiese hasta que dio caza a los tres pilotos de cabeza, Martens, Aslop y Osler. En un par de curvas fue capaz de deshacerse de ellos y cerró el triunfo entonando su frase más mítica: "'¡Simply lovely!". Max es así. “No ha sido fácil, hay gente muy rápida. Pero aproveché que había alguno muy excitado para empezar fuerte”, reconoció el tetracampeón del mundo de la clase reina. El circuito también tenía sus complicaciones, con una curva llena de agua para poner más pimienta al asunto. Aunque Verstappen es otra liga, cosa que ya ha demostrado en la F1 y en coches totalmente diferentes como los GT3. El mejor español clasificado fue Pol Tarrés, 5º clasificado. Es piloto de enduro, tiene buenos resultados en carreras de raids como la Africa Eco Race y demostró que tenía manos, aunque no alcanzó para hacer sombra a uno de los mejores pilotos de la historia de la F1. Viene del podio en Monza y Madrid, y suma su primer éxito de un 2026 en el que se cuestionó si seguiría en activo. Este es uno especial y que le recuerda a la escuela que le dio el salto a la élite. Volverá a Red Bull y la F1 con una sonrisa de oreja a oreja.

articles.title: Max vs 100: Verstappen overtakes 100 amateur karters in just 14 laps
articles.summary: Four-time F1 world champion Max Verstappen passes 100 amateur drivers in just 14 laps in an exhibition go-kart race at Silverstone.
articles.body:
Max Verstappen needed just 14 laps and 35 minutes to overtake 100 amateur drivers in an exhibition go-kart race at Silverstone.

The four-time Formula 1 world champion had a maximum of 35 laps and 75 minutes to pass everyone on an adapted track at the grand prix circuit in Northamptonshire.

Red Bull's Verstappen, 28, was up to 37th by the end of a chaotic first lap in which many drivers crashed or span out, resulting in racing being briefly suspended.

The ruthless Dutchman, who warned participants "it's not a charity event" on race radio, moved into 10th by the start of lap six and was in fourth by lap 10, with each driver who he passed having to retire.

At that stage, the field - made up of TV, sport and social media personalities, with no professional racing drivers - consisted of just Dutch F1 journalist Jacky Martens, Red Bull engine builder Lewis Osler and YouTuber Zac Alsop.

All three were given an extra 'fast lap' where they could cut a corner of the track to try to hold off Verstappen for longer, but he inevitably reeled them in.

Martens, who was on pole position after qualifying, was the final driver to be passed as Verstappen completed his challenge with 40 minutes and 21 laps to spare.

Verstappen began his racing career as a junior in karting and won four consecutive F1 titles between 2021 and 2024.

articles.title: Los gestos de Alonso son de retirada, las palabras, de continuidad
articles.standfirst: Fernando habla de la opción de seguir, pero le dijo al público antes de empezar: “No sé si es la última vez que corro en España…”
articles.summary: Fernando habla de la opción de seguir, pero le dijo al público antes de empezar: “No sé si es la última vez que corro en España…”
articles.body: El verano de Fernando Alonso ha parecido la realización de una lista de deseos antes de dejarlo todo. Ha llevado en su nuevo avión a las carreras uno a uno a sus mejores amigos. Los que llevan su museo o trabajan actualmente con él. Aquellos con los que comentábamos las carreras en los años de oro. Y a los que he celebrado volver a ver en los grandes premios. Con frases como “qué mayores estamos” o similares. La sonrisa de lo mucho vivido, la incógnita de lo mucho por hacer. También ha podido llevar a su hijo Leonard, la ilusión de su vida, a la pista en dos ocasiones, Hungaroring (donde lo metió en el box), y Madrid. Sabe que en Europa puede evitar perderse su crecimiento. Entre las cosas que quería hacer estaba correr con un casco homenaje a su primer mentor, Adrián Campos. Así lo hizo en Monza, donde se fotografió con los hijos de Adrián y elogió su labor en el automovilismo. El trasfondo real de estos ajustes con el destino sólo él lo sabe. Puede que fueran simplemente cosas que quería dejar atadas antes de tomar una decisión, por si esta es negativa. Los últimos gestos fueron los de Madring. Antes de la carrera, ante 45 mil personas en La Monumental, recibió unas preciosas palabras a su lado de Carlos Sainz: “Cuando empecé a seguir los títulos de Fernando nunca me hubiera imaginado estar aquí corriendo los dos juntos”. A continuación, el asturiano le lanzó un mensaje a los aficionados: “No sé si esta es la última vez que corro en España, así que a aprovecharlo”. Al acabar el gran premio, quiso ir muy despacio para agradecer el apoyo a los fans. Acabó la prueba por ellos, con el coche muy dañado en el toque. Se le veía emocionado, un paseo con olor a despedida… …O no, porque ya en frío, en un improvisado corralito con los medios sin derechos al que también pude asistir, afirmó que los fans merecen que siga: “Si sigo, si al final lo hago, ellos también serán un argumento para hacerlo. Primero el equipo, por supuesto, pero también los aficionados, no se merecen un final así después de todo lo que he logrado en la F-1”. Otro mensaje a favor, como el de si renuevo “no tiene porque ser sólo por un año, dos o tres”. El presidente de la FIA dice que “Fernando va a seguir”, después de insinuar antes en público que el ovetense no tiene demasiadas ganas y hay que ayudarle a que se quede. En el Tiempo de Juego de la Cadena COPE, Marc Gené aseguró que el asturiano continuará. Y de muy buena fuente. De Hungría salí optimista respecto a su permanencia en la F-1, pero ahora no lo soy tanto. El paddock está convencido de que le veremos en Bahrain 27 vestido de Aston Martin. Sin embargo, sus gestos, y el paso del tiempo, apuntan a lo contrario. Si pudiera influir en su decisión le diría, como el público de Madrid, que intentara al menos un año más. Por un último baile con el podio que endulce este amargo 2026. Eso sí, es su vida, con la íntima reflexión en la mesa de sus ganas de viajar y seguir dándolo todo por una F1 que no le llena. No tiene nada ya que demostrar. Y, haga lo que haga, lo respetaremos.

articles.title: Chase Briscoe says deer hunting gives him a bigger rush than driving 200 mph in NASCAR
articles.summary: Chase Briscoe says deer hunting now gives him a bigger adrenaline rush than NASCAR racing, and his 4-year-old son Brooks is already hooked too.
articles.body: Chase Briscoe has spent years chasing adrenaline at nearly 200 miles per hour. Apparently, that still isn’t enough. The NASCAR driver says deer hunting now gives him a rush that rivals — and may even surpass — anything he feels behind the wheel. "It’s the closest thing I’ve ever been able to come to racing, and honestly, I feel like it’s surpassed racing," Briscoe told OutKick OutDoors. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS That might sound like a bold statement coming from a NASCAR driver, but Briscoe says the explanation is actually pretty simple: racing has become normal. "You know, the racing deal, I do it so often," he said. "We race 38 weekends a year that, truthfully, the adrenaline kind of goes away because you do it all the time. "Getting to go hunting and getting to feel that adrenaline is like this drug that I can’t get rid of." Briscoe, who drives the No. 19 Bass Pro Shops Toyota, didn’t grow up as a diehard hunter. His love of the outdoors started instead around his grandfather’s pond back home in Indiana. "Ever since I was a little kid, I remember we would go over there every Sunday and would just spend time outside, out by the pond fishing," he said. Watch Chase Briscoe's full interview with OutKick OutDoors here: As he got older, fishing became a regular part of life with his friends. "Especially in my high school years, that was all me and my buddies would do," Briscoe said. "We would go find other little farm ponds or go to creeks or wherever and just go fishing." Hunting came later. After moving to North Carolina, Briscoe and his family bought roughly 30 acres that happened to be loaded with deer. A few years ago, he finally decided to give hunting a try. He was hooked almost immediately. "I went for the first time and just fell in love with it," he said. Part of the appeal is the rush. But part of it is the exact opposite. Briscoe and his wife, Marissa, have three children, and the NASCAR calendar doesn’t exactly leave much room for peace and quiet. "For me, it’s been just an amazing getaway," he said. "Just to kind of be able to get out in the outdoors and start my morning and just watch the sun come up, or just go out there and be by myself." He added: "We have three kids, and then obviously the chaos of just my career. You don’t get a lot of time just to yourself." For Chase Briscoe, hunting is a family affair These days, though, Briscoe doesn’t always hunt alone. His four-year-old son Brooks has caught the bug, too — perhaps even worse than his dad. "Brooks is ate up with it," Briscoe said. North Carolina’s deer season had just begun when Briscoe spoke with OutKick OutDoors, and the two had already been discussing their plans. "Last night we were talking about it," Briscoe said. "I said, ‘Hey, tomorrow deer season starts. I won’t be home, but Monday maybe you can go with me.’ And he was jumping up and down." Then Briscoe remembered another conversation from about a month and a half earlier. "We were just driving down the road, and he said, ‘Hey Dad, I want to talk to you about something,’" Briscoe recalled. "I was like, ‘Okay.’ He’s only 4, and he said, ‘I think this year I’m just gonna just shoot bucks this year. No more does.’" Briscoe laughed. "I’m like, ‘Okay, buddy. That sounds like a plan.’" Brooks has reason to be confident. The very first time he ever went hunting with his dad, he got a buck. "It was a total, like, one of those Hollywood stories, I guess," Briscoe said. "Literally the first time he ever went out there with me, he got a buck. "Not that it was — I mean, it was a tiny little four-pointer — but for him, it was his first experience going out there, and he got to do it." EVA SHOCKEY JOINS 'TOMI LAHREN IS FEARLESS,' DISCUSSES HUNTING AND EATING BEARS: 'NOT MY FAVORITE' Brooks helped his dad sight in the rifle and pull the trigger. The following season, Briscoe said his son took another step. "Last year, he got a doe on his own," he said. "Like, actually lined it up. I mean, I helped him, obviously — he’s 4 — but he got it right on the crosshairs and pulled the trigger." For comparison, Briscoe said it took him about a year and a half to get his first buck. "He definitely was beating me already." But for Briscoe, getting his kids into the outdoors isn’t really about who shoots the biggest buck or catches the biggest fish. It’s about the time spent together. "There’s so many distractions in today’s world with phones and tablets and TV and just everything else," Briscoe said. "For me to be able to get them outside and just get away from all those distractions. You get to spend one-on-one time and just make a lot of great memories." Those memories matter to Briscoe because he still carries his own from childhood. "I remember going fishing with my grandpa, and some of those memories are some of my favorite memories as a kid," he said. Now he gets to experience that from the other side. "To be able to be the one that’s taking my son out there and letting him have these amazing memories — he’ll always remember catching a big bass or getting that big buck," Briscoe said. "That’s just one of those core memories that you never forget." SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Go West, Briscoes Briscoe is still relatively new to hunting compared to lifelong outdoorsmen, but he’s already thinking about what comes next. "I would love to do an elk hunt," he said. "I’ve been able to do a lot of really cool whitetail hunts. Even last year, I got to go to South Texas — now two years in a row — and I’ve loved that. But I would love to go out west and do an elk hunt or even a mule deer hunt." The different terrain and challenge appeal to him, particularly the idea of getting close to an elk with a bow. "Going archery hunting for an elk, I just find that so fascinating," Briscoe said. "I think that would be one of the coolest things to do, is get an elk and get one that close." The hiking part? Maybe slightly less appealing. "I don’t know if I would enjoy that part as much," he joked. Still, Briscoe hopes he gets the chance someday. "He would have the energy too, to be hiking and walking around all the time," Briscoe said. "So yeah, if we get to do it one day, maybe he’ll go with me." articles.title: 'Sempre teve esse sonho de voar', diz amigo de piloto que morreu em SE | G1
articles.standfirst: O piloto Orácio José dos Anjos, de 61 anos, morreu após a queda de aeronave na zona rural de Macambira.
articles.summary: O piloto Orácio José dos Anjos, de 61 anos, morreu após a queda de uma aeronave em Macambira, Sergipe.
articles.body:
Orácio José dos Anjos, de 61 anos, conhecido como Chitão, morreu após a queda da aeronave que ele pilotava na zona rural do município de Macambira , a 74 km de Aracaju , nesta quinta-feira (17). Um amigo próximo dele, Fábio Reis, relatou que Orácio pilotava há cerca de cinco anos por hobby.

“Era um sonho de infância. Ele sempre teve esse sonho de voar e conseguiu realizar esse sonho. Mas um sonho que custou caro, infelizmente [...] A vida é feita de sonhos, né?”, lamentou Fábio.

Fábio também contou que eles cresceram juntos em Cícero Dantas , chegando a trabalhar juntos como camelôs, e se falavam com frequência.

O amigo também recordou um encontro entre eles, quando Orácio recebeu amigos em um aeroclube na cidade de Fátima . Na ocasião, Orácio falou o quanto estava feliz em ajudar outros pilotos.

Aeronave que caiu em Macambira (SE) e provocou a morte do piloto Orácio José dos Anjos, à direita. — Foto: Leonardo Barreto/TV Sergipe/Redes sociais

Orácio era natural de Cícero Dantas (BA) e morava em Fátima (BA), com a esposa e três dos quatro filhos. Ele também possuía um apartamento em Aracaju e era proprietário de uma funerária. Saiba quem era o piloto.

Piloto identificado como Orácio José dos Anjos, de 61 anos, que morreu após queda de aeronave em Sergipe — Foto: Fábio Reis

Piloto morre após avião de pequeno porte cair em Sergipe — Foto: Leonardo Barreto/TV Sergipe

A aeronave monomotor que Orácio pilotava caiu na zona rural do município de Macambira, a 74 km de Aracaju, no fim da manhã desta quinta-feira. Ele havia decolado do Aeroclube, na capital sergipana, por volta das 11h35, com destino a cidade de Fátima.

A Força Aérea Brasileira (FAB) informou que investigadores do Segundo Serviço Regional de Investigação e Prevenção de Acidentes Aeronáuticos (SERIPA II), órgão regional do CENIPA foram acionados para realizar a Ação Inicial da ocorrência envolvendo a aeronave de matrícula PU-SBC em Macambira.

articles.title: "Fernando Alonso me ha prometido que seguirá"
articles.standfirst: El futuro del asturiano promete ser la gran historia de final de curso tanto para Aston Martin como para su estrella
articles.summary: El futuro del asturiano promete ser la gran historia de final de curso tanto para Aston Martin como para su estrella
articles.body: Aston Martin pone toda la carne en el asador del 2027, la próxima temporada de Fórmula 1 que ya ha conocido su calendario. Todavía es temprano, pero la previsión del cuadro británico de cara a la parte final del 2026 no es del todo optimista. "No habrá más evoluciones, este año es lo que hay", radiografiaba su estrella, Fernando Alonso. Que es, precisamente, la gran incógnita que despejar para su equipo. Su continuidad o retirada en la Fórmula 1 promete ser el debate hasta final de curso.... o hasta que el bicampeón tome la palabra y anuncie su destino. Y Aston, mientras tanto, busca buenas noticias más allá. Todo está conectado. En Madrid, la última parada de la gira europea, Alonso y sus decisiones tomaron la primera plana. Pasó de cierto olor de despedida ante el público ("puede que sea mi última carrera en España") a optimismo frente a la prensa ("si renuevo puede ser por más de un año"). Y entre medias expresó que iría para largo mientras otras piezas del tablero también jugaban su papel. La más relevante es la de la FIA, representada por su presidente Mohammed Ben Sulayem, que podría abrir la mano a que Honda tenga ventajas para elevar su competitividad. Y el mandatario emiratí fue a más. "Fernando Alonso me ha prometido que seguirá", comentó. Nadie sabe, a ciencia cierta, si es por un tema del corto plazo de Aston y Honda o por el reglamento de la clase reina. El piloto de Oviedo se centra, de momento, en la salud de la propia F1. "Tenemos conversaciones a menudo con la FIA. Hay un producto que no es óptimo y se pueden hacer ajustes. Pero es independiente a que me quede, el espectáculo debe mejorar", relató en Mediaset. Si existe la posibilidad de elevar la competitividad de su proyecto, Alonso podría quedarse en un 2027 con mejores armas. Aunque en su equipo, de momento, sólo se centran en su propio trabajo. "No sé en lo que piensa [Ben Sulayem], no creo que nos pueda dar algo mágico. Nos centramos en el plan de desarrollo, trabajando duro para mejorar. Es el plan hasta la temporada. No tengo ni idea de más", explicaba Shintaro Orihara, responsable en pista de Honda. El foco es diferente en la temporada 2026. "Quedan nueve carreras en las que debemos sobrevivir a las que sean malas y aprovechar las buenas. En las próximas nos fijamos en Malasia y especialmente en Singapur", comentó Alonso. No habrá una gran evolución aerodinámica y sí apunta a una reducción de peso en las próximas citas con un motor Honda que sigue estando lejos de notar su salto. "No habrá nada grande, pero tenemos espacio para mejorar el rendimiento cambiando la calibración", destacó Orihara.

articles.title: Saffie Osborne: St Leger win has removed fear of failure for jockey
articles.summary: St Leger-winning jockey Saffie Osborne says the "fear of failure" has left her now she has won a British Classic, becoming the first woman to do so.
articles.body:
St Leger-winning jockey Saffie Osborne says the "fear of failure" has left her after she became the first woman to win a British Classic.

The 24-year-old said that despite wanting to achieve "so much more", her victory at Doncaster on Saturday means she will always be able to look back and think her career was "worth it".

Osborne said the sport can be "very lonely" - she estimates she drives 65,000 miles a year, often alone - and she has suffered some serious falls, breaking numerous bones.

But she told BBC Sport that winning one of British Flat racing's five Classics had been a dream since she was five. She has now fulfilled it.

While racing is a sport where men and women compete against one another, opportunities have not been equal.

Only six female jockeys have had rides in British Classics in 250 years, totalling 12 rides, according to the National Horseracing Museum.

They are Gay Kelleway (The Oaks, 1986; The Oaks, 1987), Alex Greaves (The Derby, 1996; 1,000 Guineas, 1996), Hayley Turner (The Derby, 2012) Josephine Gordon (1,000 Guineas, 2017), Hollie Doyle (The Oaks, 2021; St Leger, 2021; The Oaks, 2022) and Saffie Osborne (2,000 Guineas, 2024; 1,000 Guineas, 2026; St Leger, 2026).

"It has been a male-dominated sport for an extremely long time, and I suppose it's becoming less and less of a conversation, which is quite nice," she said.

"When people talk about the firsts of what women have done, I think to have my own one is quite special.

"I think it's also quite poignant because there's so few left of first things for women to do in this sport."

On Saturday's groundbreaking win, she added: "That sort of fear of failure has sort of disappeared. However much more I want to achieve, and I want to achieve so much more, it's kind of like I can always look back on my career and know that it was all worth it.

"I got to achieve what I always dreamed of achieving."

Osborne's ride on Highwayman in the St Leger was her first for trainer Joseph O'Brien, and only came about because of an injury to regular jockey Dylan Browne McMonagle.

She acknowledged that the success of a jockey is dependent on "being chosen", but is adamant that her gender isn't a factor in the opportunities she gets.

"I don't feel like in my position now that I'm ever looked at any differently because I'm a woman," she said.

"Any jockey, when you're starting out, it takes years to gain respect and be looked at as a person that people would want to use. And I don't think my gender at this point would have had anything to do with it.

"Hopefully Saturday will open more doors. But when it comes to me as a female jockey, I don't think I'm viewed any differently within the industry."

Osborne also said she is treated as "one of the lads" in the weighing room, and has never experienced sexism and misogyny unlike other female jockeys, including Bryony Frost.

Jockey Robbie Dunne was banned from racing for 18 months , with three months suspended, for bullying fellow rider Frost in 2021, which was later cut to 10 months on appeal .

Having ridden 60 winners since the start of May, Osborne is currently sitting eighth in the Flat Jockeys Championship, and is open about dreaming of being champion jockey in the future.

She would be the first female jockey to achieve that.

"You wouldn't be a jockey if you didn't want to be champion jockey one day. I think this is the first year that maybe I truly believe that I could one day," she said.

"It's been a phenomenal year that's been topped off by Saturday. But I'm very lucky. I have a very good agent [Tony Hind] and agents are so important in this sport. He's got an amazing book of jockeys, the likes of Ryan Moore, William Buick, Billy Loughnane. And I'm very lucky to be on his team.

"He makes champion jockeys, he's had a lot of them. And yeah, I would love to be the next one on the list."

articles.title: Isack Hadjar: Red Bull driver's injury recovery going to plan as team provide update on next steps ahead of Azerbaijan GP decision
articles.summary: Red Bull's Isack Hadjar has missed three races since the summer break with an injured wrist; team to assess whether Hadjar is ready to return ahead of Baku; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Hadjar has missed the last three races after sustaining a wrist injury during routine training ahead of the sport's return to action from its summer break. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson has stood in for him.

Speaking after last Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix, Mekies said Hadjar's recovery was going to plan, with a simulator session planned to help assess his readiness for any return to action in Baku.

"There is nothing wrong with Isack's recovery. I think we have learned that it's fundamentally a normal time for the sort of injuries he has," said Mekies

"So, we will continue with the same approach and what we have.

"We will evaluate the situation in a week's time.

"We have a full week, a bit more than a full week, to evaluate situations, to see how he feels and then to put him on the simulator, to expose him to real-life constraints.

"And if he feels close to 100 per cent, we go for it. If he feels the recovery is not completed, we will stick to our approach to put his recovery first.

"What we don't want to do is, by having an early return, compromise his long-term capacity to come back to 100 per cent."

The Azerbaijan GP, held on a street circuit in Baku, starts a day earlier than normal with practice taking place this coming Wednesday ahead of a Saturday race. It is the first round of a triple header with races in Malaysia and Singapore following on the subsequent two weekends.

Red Bull pleased with Lawson's 'very good' stand-in performances

Lawson has stepped up from sister Racing Bulls to cover for Hadjar, with the New Zealander returning to a seat he briefly held in an ill-fated two-race stint at the start of last season. Yuki Tsunoda has been driving for Racing Bulls.

Lawson has twice qualified eighth and scored points at both Zandvoort and Madrid, where he was sixth.

"I think he's done a very good job," said Mekies.

"I think we all know how difficult it is to jump to a different team, to a different car, and I think he has done that to the best of what could have been our expectations.

"He has taken some very important points [in Madrid] with the P6. He did the same in Zandvoort, and in Monza he would have done something similar without the contact with Nico [Hulkenberg] and the damage.

"So, I think he did a very good job. Again, very different pictures compared to the first races of 2025 when he was in the team, so we are thankful and happy with that."

Lawson has rebuilt his form and confidence at Racing Bulls over the past year and was already enjoying a consistent points-scoring season before his unexpected temporary senior Red Bull return.

"I think he has continued to grow as a driver," added Mekies, who has worked with Lawson at both Red Bull teams. "He's very calm in the car; he's very focused.

"He's certainly making... I don't know if he makes an effort or not [to do it], but he's certainly managed to keep things simple in the way he tracks with the team and in the way he tackles his own performance and the car performance.

"So, he's focused on the essentials; he tries to get the basics right, and it's working for him. Of course, with more time in the car, you can then get to another degree of finesse, maybe.

"But I think that, of course, is very, very strong."

articles.title: Lando Norris: McLaren driver reacts to Monaco Sprint news for 2027 season after Formula 1 calendar surprise
articles.summary: The Monaco Grand Prix was named as one of 10 Sprint venues on the 2027 race calendar; Norris says only one practice session will test drivers; watch every session of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from September 24-26 with a Saturday race, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
The 24-round 2027 calendar, published on Wednesday, includes 10 Sprint weekends - four more than this season - with Monaco's street circuit to host the alternative format for the first time.

The Principaliy's narrow track is not known for overtaking, where the Sprint format has hitherto tended to be used, but is considered arguably the greatest challenge in the sport for an F1 driver when it comes to qualifying.

Reacting to the news when speaking with Sky Sports F1's Natalie Pinkham alongside golfer Justin Rose during an appearance at the BMW PGA Championship Pro-Am at Wentworth on Wednesday, McLaren's Norris said: "Interesting!

"I guess the main thing is that means you've got FP1, [Sprint] qualifying on Friday - which is the challenge.

"Obviously not a lot happens in a race on Sunday or in the Sprint, but the challenge is just one practice session straight in, which has probably never happened before in Monaco."

Drivers normally have three one-hour practice sessions to build up a rhythm and momentum around the twisty wall-lined track, on which mistakes are usually heavily punished. Set-up and on-track preparation work will now all have to be squeezed into just 60 minutes.

On the new challenge that the Sprint schedule presents, Norris said: "That's more [about] relying on data from this year.

"You don't have as much time to build up to things so you're going to you're probably going have to try and risk a little bit more earlier which is normally when you can see a bit more of a difference between people who can get comfy, try things and be at 99 per cent and not go to 103 and 104 [per cent] because in Monaco when you go to that limit, game over.

"It's more exciting for the fans and the people watching."

Norris won the Monaco Grand Prix from pole position in 2025 during his title-winning year.

articles.title: Fernando Alonso sigue presionando a Honda
articles.standfirst: El piloto asturiano, Fernando Alonso, pide a Aston Martin que se centren en mejorar la Unidad de Potencia
articles.summary: El piloto asturiano, Fernando Alonso, pide a Aston Martin que se centren en mejorar la Unidad de Potencia
articles.body: Fernando Alonso, tiene claro que el problema a mejorar en su Aston Martin es el motor y por ello le pide a los ingleses que se centren en él. El Gran Premio de España tuvo que haber sido uno de los más especiales para el asturiano y sin embargo acabó siendo un desastre: "El motor ha sido muy malo," declaraba Fernando a los medios tras la carrera. Cruzando la línea de meta 17º, a dos vueltas del ganador, Kimi Antonelli, el piloto de Aston Martin sabe que las mejoras en su rendimiento son cuestión de motor y no tanto de conducción, cuyos problemas iniciales han ido mejorando, así como el asturiano ha declarado. "Creo que hoy me ha costado controlar el turbo, y casi se me cala el motor en las paradas en boxes y también en algunas de las banderas azules, al dejar pasar a los demás y reducir la velocidad", declaraba el bicampeón al finalizar la carrera. Tal y como Fernando ha explicado, no solo era que el motor en sí no tuviera apenas potencia, sino que además al motor le costaba recuperarla tras reducir la velocidad, por lo que pide a su equipo y a Honda que investiguen qué ha sucedido. Mientras los problemas en Aston Martin continúan y ellos intenta solucionarlos, la continuidad de Fernando sigue siendo un tema que mantiene a todos pendientes. Tal y como Mike Krack, responsable de pista de Aston Martin, declaraba, la no continuidad de Fernando sería impensable y dramático. Sin embargo, desde el equipo inglés entienden el tiempo que Fernando se está tomando en decidir finalmente su futuro: "Al fin y al cabo, siempre hemos dejado claro que el equipo quiere seguir (con él), pero tenemos que respetar la opinión de Fernando y el tiempo que quiera tomarse," declaraba Krack. Tanta es la necesidad de la continuidad de Fernando, que hasta el presidente de la FIA, Mohammed Ben Sulayem, habló con Fernando durante el Gran Premio de España en busca de una solución que beneficie a Aston Martin para que el asturiano siga en el mundial unas cuantas temporadas más. Entre esos beneficios sería la ayuda de Mercedes a Honda y, por consiguiente, a Aston Martin, tal y como Toto Wolff, CEO de Mercede F1 Team, declaró, al no verlo tan descabellado ya que, según afirma, en este deporte, cuando el reglamento cambia, es necesario una serie de modificaciones para que pueda haber una mayor competitividad y de esta manera el deporte no se estanque y pueda seguir avanzando. No obstante, Fernando sigue jugando con las especulaciones de su futuro. Mientras que por un lado amenaza con retirarse tras cada fin de semana, cuyo desastre vuelve siempre a aparecer, y acaba cansado del "campeonato mundial de baterías" tal y como describe a la nueva F1, también dedica palabras a su continuidad, y no precisamente por un corto periodo de tiempo. En Aston Martin no le dan por perdido, centrando todos sus esfuerzos en revertir a situación y darle el mejor monoplaza al asturiano para que éste sea capaz de luchar por mejores posiciones: "Como ya he dicho antes, estamos seguros de que podemos llegar a una buena solución para todos. Ahora solo queda esperar. Él tiene que decidirse y, después, seguiremos adelante," declaraba Mike Kraft.

articles.title: Isack Hadjar sigue siendo duda para Azerbaiyán
articles.standfirst: El piloto de Red Bull sigue con su recuperación y desde el equipo inglés no dan una fecha exacta para su regreso a la competición
articles.summary: El piloto de Red Bull sigue con su recuperación y desde el equipo inglés no dan una fecha exacta para su regreso a la competición
articles.body: Isack Hadjar sigue con su recuperación a la espera de su reincorporación a la competición, posiblemente en Azerbaiyán la próxima semana. El piloto de Red Bull Racing se ha perdido las tres últimas citas tras su lesión en la muñeca al fracturársela practicando boxeo como entrenamiento, perdiéndose así los Grandes Premios de Países Bajos, Italia y España. A pesar de ser muchos puntos perdidos, la prioridad en Red Bull es la completa recuperación de piloto francés antes de volver a subirse al monoplaza, tal y como ha afirmado su jefe de equipo, Laurent Mekies, a Sky Sports F1: "No hay ningún problema con la recuperación de Isack. Creo que hemos aprendido que, en esencia, es un plazo normal para el tipo de lesiones que tiene." Una recuperación esencial y básica que hasta Marc Márquez recomendó al piloto de Red Bull Racing se tomase su tiempo, aconsejándole que no corriese lesionado. A esto, Hadjar le tomó la palabra y prefirió no correr ya en Países Bajos, arrastrando también Monza y Madring. Liam Lawson ha sido el encargado de reemplazar a Isack Hadjar en el equipo oficial, cediendo a la vez su asiento a Yuki Tsunoda, quien regresaba de esta forma a la competición. Mientras Liam ha puntuado en dos de las tres carreras que ha disputado como sustituto, quedando 7º en Zandvoort y 6º en Madring. Laurent Mekies describía así las actuaciones de Lawson, l micrófono de Sky Sport F1: "Ha sumado puntos muy importantes en Madrid con el P6 e hizo lo mismo en Zandvoort. En Monza habría conseguido algo parecido de no ser por el contacto con Nico (Hülkenberg) y los daños." A pesar de que haya un alto porcentaje de que Hadjar pueda reaparecer en Azerbaiyán, desde Red Bull tienen muy claro que precipitarse sería un grave error que podría no hacer más que agravar la lesión de su piloto, tal y como Mekies ha comentado al medio inglés: "Si se siente casi al 100 por ciento, nos lanzamos a por ello. Si considera que aún no se ha recuperado del todo, nos ceñiremos a nuestro enfoque de dar prioridad a su recuperación. Lo que no queremos es que, al volver antes de tiempo, ponga en peligro su capacidad a largo plazo para recuperarse al 100 %" Es por ello que desde Red Bull Racing no dan una fecha exacta al regreso de Hadjar y prefieren tomarse su tiempo antes de tomar una decisión precipitada. Según afirma Mikeis, aún cuentan con el tiempo suficiente para decidir si su piloto vuelve en Azerbaiyán o, por el contrario, siguen esperando un poco más.

articles.title: Mike Elliott: Former Mercedes design boss Elliott joins Alpine as chief technical officer
articles.summary: Former Mercedes F1 design boss Mike Elliott joins Alpine as chief technical officer.
articles.body:
Former Mercedes Formula 1 design boss Mike Elliott has joined Alpine as chief technical officer.

The 52-year-old will "lead and oversee the technical and engineering functions at the team's factory in Enstone", a statement said.

Elliott's recruitment is the latest step in Alpine's attempt to return to competitiveness after slumping to the back of the field in 2025.

The move marks a return to the team for Elliott, who was principal aerodynamicist there from 2008-12 when the outfit was known as Renault and then Lotus.

Elliott then spent more than a decade at Mercedes through their dominant years with Lewis Hamilton, rising from head of aerodynamics to technical director and then chief technical officer.

An Alpine statement said: "Elliott has a proven track record in the sport, having contributed to an impressive eight constructors' and eight drivers' championships.

"Elliott's arrival at Enstone strengthens the team's technical capabilities as the team looks to build on the improved performances on track and close the gap to the top four teams."

F1 to have 10 sprint races in 2027, including Monaco

Verstappen passes 100 amateur karters in 14 laps

Elliott takes his place in the team's engineering structure above executive technical director David Sanchez, who joined in May 2024.

The statement contained no remarks either from executive adviser Flavio Briatore, the team's de facto boss, or managing director Steve Nielsen, their effective team principal.

Elliott will start work at the team's factory in Enstone, Oxfordshire, next week and Briatore and Nielsen will address his hiring publicly at the next race, the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on 24-26 September.

Elliott, whose career in F1 started at McLaren in 2000, left Mercedes under something of a cloud in October 2023, after the design philosophy the team pursued under his leadership for the 'ground-effect' era from 2022-25 proved a failure.

Eliott had taken on the role of technical director from the highly regarded James Allison and led work on the 2022 design, with Allison moving into a more senior role overseeing the wider company as chief technical officer.

Mercedes followed what became known as a 'zero-pod' concept, where the sidepods were pared back to almost nothing as part of an aerodynamic philosophy that aimed to run the car as close to the ground as possible.

In the wind tunnel, it produced prodigious downforce. But the concept was prone to a phenomenon known as 'porpoising', where the airflow stalls under the floor and sets up a high-frequency bouncing motion.

All the teams suffered from this to a degree in early 2022, but Mercedes found it harder than most to get on top of it.

Although Red Bull dominated the 2022 season with a different design concept, which used heavily undercut side pods to channel airflow used to 'seal' the floor, Mercedes stuck to their guns for 2023, convinced the design could be made to work. The decision came against the pleas of Hamilton to change tack.

When the 2023 car was also off the pace, Elliott swapped roles with Allison.

The move was presented by Mercedes as Elliott's own idea, but within six months he had left the company - again, Mercedes said it was Elliott's decision.

The Alpine role is his first in F1 since leaving Mercedes, and it sees him rejoin forces with Briatore and Nielsen, who were both there during Elliott's first spell with the team.

articles.title: Samantha Busch says Ty Gibbs has been like a 'big brother' to Brexton in recent months
articles.summary: Ty Gibbs, who also lost his father abruptly at a young age has "been a source of comfort" for Brexton Busch
articles.body:
This weekend, Ty Gibbs will carry the M&Ms colors in honor of NASCAR legend Kyle Busch at Bristol Motor Speedway, a track he dominated at.

Busch, who died suddenly at just 41 years old in May, earned most of his success at Joe Gibbs Racing with M&Ms as his primary sponsor, including two championships in 2015 and 2019.

Kyle's wife Samantha has been very open about the struggles she and her family have endured while trying to cope with the tragic loss of Kyle due to a severe case of pneumonia that progressed in sepsis just before this year's Coca-Cola 600.

In a new post on her Instagram page, Samantha offered details on just how much the Gibbs family has been there for the Busch family in these trying months.

She recalled a moment when she was struggling with panic attacks, and asked for Heather Gibbs to come over. Heather had to deal with her own unimaginable loss when husband Coy Gibbs died abruptly in the hours following Ty's 2022 NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series championship. He was 49 years old at the time of his passing.

Richard Childress, Samantha Busch, Brexton Busch, Lennix Busch, NASCAR CEO Steve O'Donnell

"I just wanted to really take a moment to explain to you guys like just how much NASCAR is a family," said Samantha. "So when everything happened, I don't know what day it was -- I was having a lot of panic attacks and just freaking out and somebody was like, what do you need? And I was like, 'someone call Heather. I need Heather right now.' And I remember she came to the house right away and I just thought, okay, she's somebody who's going to understand. She went from the high of highs -- Ty won his championship to the next day, Coy was gone, and I felt like it was so similar. We had the kid's birthday parties and all these great things, and then Kyle's gone. I just remember her sitting downstairs in the basement with me and I was just crying and panicking, and and she was there for me."

Samantha went on to reveal that it didn't stop with emotional support from Heather alone, as her and Coy's son Ty has been spending time with Brexton and acting almost as a 'big brother' to Kyle's 11-year-old, who continues his own journey up the racing ladder even after Kyle's passing. Ty was just 20 when his father Coy died, only a few hours after he won the 2022 NASCAR O'Reilly Series championship at Phoenix.

"I can't even put no words how wonderful he's been to Brexton," said Samantha in regards to Ty. "He's been like a big brother. He's been a source of comfort for him. I mean, Ty's still young himself and he has come over. He's taken Brexton to lunch, he's rode karts around our neighborhood with him, he came and picked him up and took him to breakfast and took him to the track to race karts. NASCAR is family. Ty knows what it's like."

She also remembered how similar Coy and Kyle were in the years working together at JGR, as both were "blunt, shoot you straight" types.

"Gosh, I think for Brexton to have Ty to understand exactly what he's going through -- he came home one day from hanging out with Ty and he was like, 'we talked about our dads.' He just comes home so much happier."

She went on to thank M&Ms, their parent company Mars, and JGR for this incredible tribute that Ty will carry on the No. 54 Toyota this weekend.

"..I am so grateful that this has been the hardest time of our lives but from not only people within the sport, but the fans, everybody. I'll never be able to put into words how awful and horrific the situation is but equally so, how amazing and just the amount of love. It's hard for my brain to process, so it's even harder for me to explain but it's amazing. All that said just really grateful to Mars and to JGR for putting this together. Kyle was the 'Candy Man,' there was a lot of amazing memories. So much of the stuff I think about is with him in that yellow M&Ms fire suit.

I think it's gonna be really hard to see it on the track, but really iconic and special at the same time. So, see you all Saturday night."

articles.title: Driverless racing goes global. Will fans care?
articles.summary: Autonomous race cars hit Laguna Seca and Imola Circuit at speeds topping 157 mph, but the Abu Dhabi Autonomous Racing League faces a fan problem.
articles.body: Autonomous race cars are starting to show up on some very famous tracks. On Sept. 3, the Indy Autonomous Challenge brought its driverless race cars to WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca in California. Purdue AI Racing set a new autonomous track record and finished second in a head-to-head passing competition. Italy's Unimore Racing took the win. Two days later, autonomous racing took another step forward in Europe. Five teams brought fully autonomous race cars to Italy's Imola Circuit for the Abu Dhabi Autonomous Racing League's first race outside Abu Dhabi. Team Kinetiz came from fourth on the grid to win the 12-lap event. Now autonomous racing has reached major circuits in the U.S., Europe and Abu Dhabi. The technology clearly travels. The bigger question is whether the fans will follow. NEW! Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better Healthcare With AI In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you take a more active role in your healthcare. You’ll learn how to organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare questions for your next doctor’s visit. No technical experience is needed. Register for free now at CyberGuyLive.com WAYMO RECALLS ROBOTAXIS OVER CONSTRUCTION-ZONE RISK Driverless racing is becoming a global competition The races at Laguna Seca and Imola came from two different autonomous racing programs. The Indy Autonomous Challenge brings together university teams that develop AI drivers for identical race cars. At Laguna Seca, nine university teams from North America, Europe and Asia were scheduled to compete. The Sept. 3 event pushed the competition further by adapting the Indy Autonomous Challenge's passing format to a road course for the first time. Instead of several cars racing as a pack, two autonomous cars take turns in attacking and defending roles. The software has to manage spacing and decide when it can safely make a move. Purdue became the only American team to qualify for that portion of the competition. Its car also set a 1:27.731 autonomous lap record before finishing runner-up to Unimore. Then came Imola. A2RL brought autonomous racing from its home at Yas Marina Circuit in Abu Dhabi to Europe for the first time. The league says Imola represents another step toward its goal of creating an international championship for fully autonomous race cars. Five autonomous race cars headed to the grid at Imola Imola raised the difficulty again. Kinetiz, Constructor Racing, PoliMOVE, Unimore Racing and two-time A2RL champion TUM entered the event. Each team competed with identical EAV-25 race car hardware based on the Dallara Super Formula SF23 platform. That means much of the competitive advantage came from the software each team developed. The AI had to figure out where the car was, understand what was happening around it and decide what to do next. Then it had to turn those decisions into braking and steering inputs at racing speed. TUM ran into a technical problem on the formation lap and returned to the pits before the rolling start. That left the remaining cars to fight for position. Unimore had started from pole and led the race. Then things went wrong. WAYMO VEHICLES 'PUTTING AMERICAN LIVES AT RISK,' SOURCE WARNS AMID AUTONOMOUS VEHICLE COMPANY'S MASSIVE RECALL A crash showed how hard autonomous racing can be Unimore set the fastest lap of the race before suffering a technical problem that caused the car to slow dramatically. PoliMOVE was close behind and hit the slowing Unimore car from the rear. The collision ended both teams' runs. That opened the door for Kinetiz. The Singapore-UAE team had started fourth but moved into the lead and won by 10.963 seconds over Germany's Constructor Racing. PoliMOVE was classified third. The crash may also be one of the most revealing parts of the race. Driving fast on an empty track is one challenge. Reacting when the car directly in front of you suddenly loses speed creates a much harder problem. That is exactly the type of unpredictability autonomous systems have to learn to handle. These AI race cars are getting seriously fast These cars are moving a lot faster than you might expect. At Imola, PoliMOVE hit about 157 mph with nobody behind the wheel. During testing, the fastest autonomous lap came within 0.85 seconds of a benchmark lap set by Super Formula driver Juju Noda. That is surprisingly close. In Abu Dhabi last year, former Formula 1 driver Daniil Kvyat still set a faster lap than the autonomous challenger, but the gap had narrowed to just 1.58 seconds. So the question has changed. We already know these cars can get around a race track at serious speeds. Now we are seeing what happens when they have to race another car and make those decisions in real time. But who are fans supposed to root for? Here's where autonomous racing faces a challenge that has nothing to do with speed. Part of the fun of racing is having someone to root for. Fans follow drivers, get to know their personalities and pick favorites. Take the driver out of the car and suddenly that connection looks very different. With autonomous racing, you are rooting for the team behind the software. For some tech fans, that may be enough. Watching engineers figure out how to make an AI-powered race car faster and smarter could become part of the appeal. But will people come back race after race? We are already starting to get a sense of that. The Indy Autonomous Challenge returned to Laguna Seca this year and moved from solo time trials in 2025 to head-to-head passing on the road course. Just two days later, five autonomous race cars competed together at Imola in Italy. Now the harder part may be building the kind of connection that keeps people watching after the surprise of seeing an empty cockpit wears off. So what is the point of racing cars without drivers? There is another reason these competitions are worth watching. Race tracks give autonomous driving researchers a place to push software extremely hard. At Laguna Seca, Purdue's team spent weeks practicing and used simulation to find bugs in its software before race day. At Imola, the AI had to deal with high speeds and other autonomous cars making their own decisions. That pressure can reveal weaknesses quickly. A passenger car on a public road faces a very different environment. It has to deal with pedestrians, intersections and countless situations that do not exist on a closed race track. So winning an autonomous race does not mean the same software is ready to drive you around town. Still, the basic challenge overlaps. An autonomous vehicle has to understand what is happening around it and decide how to respond. Racing forces researchers to test those capabilities at the edge of what the vehicle can handle. That is where this becomes relevant even if you never watch a single autonomous race. Kurt's key takeaways Here's what gets me about autonomous racing. We have gone from asking whether AI can keep a race car on the track to watching these cars chase each other at more than 150 mph. That is pretty remarkable. But speed alone will not turn this into a sport people care about. Part of what makes racing so compelling is the person inside the car. You follow the driver, learn their personality and pick someone you want to win. When the cockpit is empty, that connection changes completely. Could fans eventually start rooting for the teams behind the technology instead? I can see Purdue students and engineers developing their own following as these competitions grow. But autonomous racing still has to prove that watching great software compete can be as exciting as watching a great driver push a car to the limit. The cars are clearly ready to race. Now we get to see whether the fans are ready to care. Would you watch an entire race with nobody behind the wheel?
